_note: The lane catalogue and the rotation profiles, in one file. This is the SOURCE OF TRUTH: config/profiles/*.json are generated from it by make_profiles.py and must never be hand-edited. Every frequency here is a US/international allocation rather than a local one, so this file is usable as-is almost anywhere in the US; what differs by location lives in stations.json.

0.label: LOW BAND 118-174 MHz -- set dipole ~50cm, or fit a discone
0._serial_note: Pin every radio by SERIAL. librtlsdr index order is not stable across a replug, and a swapped index presents as bad reception, never as an error. List yours with 'rtl_test -t'; set them with 'rtl_eeprom -d 0 -s 00000001'. Two dongles reporting the same serial is the default from the factory and must be fixed before anything here is trustworthy.

1.label: HIGH BAND 225-1090 MHz -- set dipole ~17cm, or fit a discone

guard_121.note: 121.500 international aviation DISTRESS. Expected silent; a recording here matters.

milair_guard.note: 243.000 MILITARY guard/distress. The UHF twin of 121.5.

air_tower_voice.note: Your local tower and approach. Channels within ~1.5 MHz land in one slice and are heard simultaneously.

air_ground_voice.note: Your local ground control. Usually too far from tower to share a slice.

milair_voice.note: UHF military air, AM and unencrypted. DISABLED until you seed real frequencies from milair_survey -- the shipped placeholders will hear nothing.

murs_voice.note: MURS 151.82/151.88/151.94 -- retail and warehouse handhelds, unencrypted NFM. US allocation.

frs_voice.note: All 15 FRS/GMRS 462 channels at once (175 kHz block). 'Privacy codes' are CTCSS squelch tones, NOT encryption.

vhf_fire.note: VHF fire mutual-aid, where it is still simulcast in the clear. DISABLED by default: on the author's site this produced ZERO audio in 317 runs at both 11 dB and 7 dB squelch, which is a coverage answer, not a bug. Confirm a carrier with a sweep before enabling.

air_survey.note: Airband occupancy 118-137. Discovers which channels are live before you record them.

airband_survey.note: Narrower airband sweep for the high-band radio.

noaa_wx.note: NOAA weather radio 162.4-162.55. KNOWN-GOOD CONTROL: it transmits 24/7, so this lane must ALWAYS show a carrier. If it goes quiet, the radio is broken, not the band.

survey_fm.note: FM broadcast. KNOWN-GOOD CONTROL for the high-band radio -- carriers must always appear. Every station needs at least one lane whose silence is unambiguous.

frs_survey.note: FRS/GMRS 462 occupancy. Redundant while frs_voice runs; useful to find which channels are worth the dwell.

milair_survey.note: Military air 225-400 MHz occupancy. 175 MHz of spectrum -- rtl_power hops it. This is how you find real frequencies for milair_voice.

p25_survey.note: 700 MHz public-safety occupancy. Finds carriers only. Whether those talkgroups are encrypted is a separate question this project does not attempt to answer, and never attempts to defeat.

lora915.note: 902-928 ISM occupancy: LoRa, utility telemetry, and everything else sharing the band.

tpms315.note: 315 MHz TPMS -- tyre pressure sensors on passing vehicles. A TPMS id identifies a TYRE SENSOR, never a person. See docs/COVERAGE.md before doing anything with these.

ism433.note: 433.92 ISM: weather stations, doorbells, remotes, and 315 MHz TPMS's European twin.

adsb.note: 1090 MHz ADS-B. Squawk 7500/7600/7700 is a STRUCTURED emergency signal -- it beats any transcript, because it cannot be misheard.

uat978.note: 978 MHz UAT -- the US general-aviation half of ADS-B, invisible to a 1090-only receiver.

pagers.note: POCSAG/FLEX 929.6 -- dispatch traffic in PLAIN TEXT. No ASR cost, and no transcription error possible.

aprs.note: 144.390 ham APRS position/telemetry. DISABLED until direwolf is installed and configured.

acars.note: 131.550 aircraft text. DISABLED until acarsdec is built -- see patches/acarsdec-macos.patch.sh.

profiles.name: watch-day
profiles.description: Daytime default. Weighted to air, emergency, handhelds and military air. Both radios rotate; the two guard channels and the FRS block get the longest dwells.

profiles.name: watch-night
profiles.description: Overnight. Air traffic collapses after ~23:00, so airband shrinks and the radios lean toward handhelds, vehicles and sensors. Both guards stay.

profiles.name: event-air
profiles.description: EVENT: aviation. Tower pinned on one radio, military air on the other. Nothing else is heard while this runs -- that is the point, and it is also the cost.

profiles.name: event-emergency
profiles.description: EVENT: emergency watch. Both distress guards plus pager dispatch and the 700 MHz sweep. The narrowest, loudest configuration.

profiles.name: event-walkie
profiles.description: EVENT: handhelds. MURS pinned low, all 15 FRS/GMRS channels pinned high. Maximum handheld capture, zero survey.
